newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-ZIMBABWE WAIT ON GROBBELAAR'S ARRIVAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ZIMBABWE WAIT ON GROBBELAAR'S ARRIVAL.

text.p: Zimbabwe are standing by for the arrival of goalkeeper Bruce Grobbelaar for their vital African Nations' Cup group one match against Ghana on Sunday.
The match in Harare is one of 12 internationals to be played on the continent this weekend.
Grobbelaar is standing trial on match-fixing charges in Britain but Zimbabwean officials say they have received permission for him to travel for the match.
"I contacted the judge and he said it was okay for Bruce to come," said Zimbabwe F.A. secretary-general Phil Hwata.
"We are very keen for him to play," said coach Ian Porterfield. "It's going to be a tough game. We have a lot of respect for the Ghanaians."
Zimbabwe are starting their qualifying campaign afresh after their 3-0 away win over Sudan in October was annulled when the Sudanese withdrew from the competition last week.
Elsewhere, Zambia attempt to arrest an alarming slump in form that could well mark the end of the glittering international career of captain Kalusha Bwalya.

They travel to neighbouring Malawi on Saturday. The group seven clash is filled with all the traditional rivalry of neighbours but is given added importance by Zambia's desire to rediscover the form that saw them finish as Africa's second-best team on the FIFA rankings last year.
They will also be without captain Kalusha Bwalya, the inspirational midfielder who helped rebuild the Zambian team after 18 players died in an air crash almost four years ago.

Bwalya, long the undisputed leader of the Zambian team, has come in for heavy criticism in the last two weeks following the home side's failure to beat arch rivals South Africa at home in a World Cup qualifier earlier this month.
He has been accused in the Zambian press of causing division in the side by insisting on helping to pick the team along with acting coach Freddie Mwila.
Club commitments in Mexico have ruled the 33-year-old out of the game, giving midfielder Charles Musonda a chance to take over the running of the team.
Malawi's coach Reuben Malola has been watching the furore with interest and says he is confident his young team can upset Zambia.

Ethiopia, who were due to play Morocco in Casablanca on Sunday, have had their group three match postponed after 16 players defected from the squad in transit in Rome and applied for political asylum.
Ethiopia are still to decide whether they intend continuing in the qualifiers.

Sierra Leone are at home in group four against the Central African Republic, who will be allowed to play despite having their club teams disqualified from this year's three African club competitions for the non-payment of outstanding debts to the Federation of African Football.
Cameroon line up against group five lightweights Namibia without suspended striker Alphonse Tchami.
Liberia will again be without injured George Weah for their group six match in Accra against Togo.
